name: The Queen Of Puddings
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: one half cup jelly or jam
ingredients.originalText: one half cup jelly or jam
ingredients.quantityText: one half cup jelly or jam

instructions.text: Rub the butter into a cup of sugar; beat the yolks very light, and stir these together to a cream.
Add the bread-crumbs, soaked in milk, then the seasoning.
Bake this in a buttered pudding-dish—a large one and but two-thirds full—until the custard is "set."
Draw to the mouth of the oven, spread over with jam or other nice fruit-conserve.
Cover this with a méringue made of the whipped whites and half a cup of sugar.
Shut the oven and bake until the méringue begins to color.

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Rub the butter into a cup of sugar; beat the yolks very light, and stir these together to a cream.
2. Add the bread-crumbs, soaked in milk, then the seasoning.
3. Bake this in a buttered pudding-dish—a large one and but two-thirds full—until the custard is "set."
4. Draw to the mouth of the oven, spread over with jam or other nice fruit-conserve.
5. Cover this with a méringue made of the whipped whites and half a cup of sugar.
6. Shut the oven and bake until the méringue begins to color.
7. Eat cold, with cream.
